Introduction
We appreciate your interest in helping secure Vercel Sandbox. This is a time-boxed public bug bounty focused on the Sandbox isolation boundary: the Firecracker microVM, the host-side sandbox firewall, credential brokering, and the sandbox control plane API.
This is not the Vercel platform bug bounty and not the Vercel open-source program. Do not report vercel.com, v0, dashboard, general platform bugs; or anything unrelated to Vercel Sandbox. Submit those to the appropriate Vercel HackerOne programs.

Bounties are paid per report, scoped to a single root cause. Severity is assigned by Vercel triage based on the maximum demonstrable impact of that root cause ; not the reporter's self-assessment and not CVSS alone. A single report is paid at the severity of the highest-impact variant demonstrated.
Valid reports that inflate severity without a detailed rationale aligned with this bounty table will have the bounty reduced by 25%.
Severity	Bounty (USD)	Typical impact
Critical	$25,000 – $50,000	MicroVM → EC2 host escape, or cross-tenant read / modify / RCE
High	$10,000 – $25,000	Firewall bypass with credential or data exfil, or cross-tenant DoS
Medium	$5,000 – $10,000	Policy boundary violation without demonstrated secret exfil
Low	$1,000 – $5,000	Hardening gaps, oracles
The $50,000 maximum is for a vulnerability that lets a threat actor read or modify information belonging to another Vercel tenant. Partial impact is paid at the partial tier. Multiple reports that share one root cause: only the first valid, fully reproducible report is eligible.
AI slop and out of scope submissions will receive no bug bounty payout and will be marked as Not Applicable or Spam. This includes reports that appear to be generated by AI tools without manual validation, contain hallucinated or unverified claims, or consist of scanner output without a working exploit.

Introduction
ASSA ABLOY Opening Solutions Americas and/or any of its group companies (together or individually, "ASSA ABLOY Americas") believes that the disclosure of vulnerabilities is essential to improving the quality of our products and services. ASSA ABLOY Americas values the insights of the security research community and welcomes disclosure and collaboration.
Through our responsible disclosure process, ASSA ABLOY Americas will work with security researchers and other vulnerability investigators to make our products and services more secure by providing a mechanism to privately report vulnerabilities with legitimacy and integrity. Responsible disclosure ensures that security infrastructure is tested and proven reliable. This process allows us to work collaboratively with researchers to identify and mitigate vulnerabilities quickly in an ever-changing security environment.
We appreciate your contributions to protecting our customers, users, and businesses.

Please sign up for your own accounts using your @wearehackerone.com email address.
Out of Scope
Please note that we cannot authorize out-of-scope testing on third-party products or services. Vulnerabilities discovered in third-party products or services should be reported to the appropriate vendor.

HTML Injection
Rate limiting
HTTP headers without an associated, exploitable vulnerability
Reporting
Please use the Report Vulnerability tab to submit a finding, or visit our partner HackerOne at https://hackerone.com/vulnerability-rating-taxonomy.
Disclosure
ASSA ABLOY Americas will follow standard industry practices for coordinated and responsible vulnerability disclosure. We ask all vulnerability reporters to do the same — please allow ASSA ABLOY Americas the opportunity to verify and remediate reported vulnerabilities and to notify affected customers and users before you disclose or share the vulnerability or exploitation methods with any third party.
ASSA ABLOY Americas product security advisories will be made publicly available at https://www.assaabloydss.com/en/resource-center/security-center/product-security-advisories and/or communicated directly to affected customers.
Safe Harbor
ASSA ABLOY believes that ethical security research performed in good faith provides an invaluable public service and has therefore provided this safe harbor program to encourage lawful, authorized security testing of our products and services.
Accordingly, ASSA ABLOY will not initiate, pursue, or recommend any law enforcement or civil lawsuits related to the specific actions taken by you to discover a security vulnerability, provided that such actions were undertaken in good faith, for the sole purpose of improving the overall security of our products and services, and not for any nefarious or otherwise unlawful purpose.

Response Targets
Omnicell Corporation will make reasonable efforts to meet the following response

Do not discuss this program or any vulnerabilities (even resolved ones) outside of the program without express consent from the organization.

Program Rules
Please submit detailed reports that include reproducible steps. Reports that do
not contain enough detail to reproduce the issue will not be eligible for a reward.
Provide technical details of the vulnerability or concern, such as:
URLs or systems impacted, including software version, if applicable
Additional information that will be helpful to us such as details of testing
environment and tools used to discover vulnerabilities
Discovery method, when, where, how
Submit one vulnerability per report, unless multiple vulnerabilities must be
chained together to demonstrate impact.
In the event of duplicate reports, only the first report received will be eligible for
an award, provided the issue can be fully reproduced.
Multiple vulnerabilities that stem from a single underlying root cause will be
eligible for a single acknowledgment only.
Social engineering, including phishing, vishing, and smishing, is prohibited.

interruption or degradation. Only interact with accounts you own or for which you

Keep requests to Omnicell web servers to a minimum.
Omnicell Employees or contractors (past and current) and their associates/family
members are not eligible.
Out of Scope Vulnerabilities
When submitting vulnerability reports, please consider both the attack scenario or
exploitability and the security impact of the issue. The following are considered out of
scope:
Clickjacking on pages that do not perform sensitive actions.
Unauthenticated, logout, or login CSRF.
Attacks that require a machine-in-the-middle position or physical access to a
user’s device.
Previously known vulnerable libraries without a working proof of concept.
CSV injection without a demonstrated vulnerability impact.
Missing SSL/TLS best-practice configurations including weak cipher suites, TLS
versions.
Minor CORS misconfiguration without data exposure.
Any activity that could disrupt service availability, including DoS.
Content spoofing or text injection issues that do not demonstrate an attack vector
or the ability to modify HTML/CSS.
Rate-limiting or brute-force issues on non-authentication endpoints.
Missing Content Security Policy best practices.
Missing HttpOnly or Secure cookie flags.
Missing email security best practices, including invalid, incomplete, or missing
SPF, DKIM, or DMARC records.
Vulnerabilities that affect only outdated or unpatched browsers that are fewer

📜 The Rules of Engagement: Our VDP Guidelines
Welcome, researchers! To ensure a productive and positive partnership, we've established the following guidelines for our Vulnerability Disclosure Program. We ask that you read and adhere to these rules throughout your testing.
✈️ Our Core Principles: Your Code of Conduct
Your trust is essential to us. We expect all researchers to act in good faith and uphold the highest ethical standards.
Testing Window: Please limit all research and testing from Monday 2PM GMT to Friday 11PM GMT
Rule Description
Act in Good Faith Your activities should be focused on finding and reporting vulnerabilities, not disrupting, damaging, or harming Gogo, our systems, our data, or our users.
Protect Our Data Exfiltrating or copying any data is strictly prohibited. Your testing should be limited to verifying the existence of a vulnerability.
Respect User Privacy You must not access, modify, or compromise the data or privacy of our customers or employees. Only interact with accounts you own or for which you have explicit, documented permission.
🔧 Technical Guidelines for Testing
To ensure the stability of our services, please follow these technical rules.
Identify Yourself: Please add a custom HTTP header to all your testing traffic. This helps our team distinguish your research from malicious activity.
Header: X-HackerOne-Research: [Your-H1-Username]
Responsible Automated Scanning: Automated scanning is welcome, but it must be throttled to a reasonable rate to avoid impacting our services. As a guideline, please limit requests to 10 requests per second. Excessive scanning may lead to your IP being blocked.
DO NOT submit ANY forms within ANY Gogo systems.
📝 Reporting & Disclosure: How to Work With Us
Clear communication is key to a successful VDP.
Prompt & Detailed Reports: Report any potential vulnerability to us promptly through the HackerOne platform. High-quality reports are essential for our team to validate and fix issues.
Your report must include:
Detailed, Reproducible Steps: If we cannot reproduce the issue, we cannot triage it.
One Vulnerability Per Report: Please submit a single, distinct vulnerability in each report. The only exception is when chaining vulnerabilities is necessary to demonstrate impact.
First-to-Find: We operate on a first-come, first-served basis. When duplicate vulnerabilities are reported, we will only award the first reproducible report received.

Previously known vulnerable libraries without a working Proof of Concept

Missing best practices in SSL/TLS configuration

Vulnerabilities only affecting users of outdated or unpatched browsers (less than 2 stable versions behind the latest released stable version)
Software version disclosure / Banner identification issues / Descriptive error messages or headers (e.g. stack traces, application or server errors)
Tabnabbing
Open redirect - unless an additional security impact can be demonstrated
Issues that require unlikely user interaction
